features: THE CODE NOBODY REMEMBERS BY HEART — One migration: the database is touched. It adds a new table, the list of Italian municipalities, and modifies no existing data. No column of the program is linked to that list: it is a help, not a constraint. This version closes the fifth and last report of the series that arrived on the forum on 18 August — the only one that was not a defect.

FOUR FIELDS TYPED BY HAND EVERY TIME. A municipality's cadastral code — «H501» for Rome, «E602» for Linguaglossa — is exactly the kind of data nobody remembers and everybody looks up elsewhere every time. Now next to the «Cadastral municipality» field there is a small button: you type the name, pick from the list, and two fields get filled instead of one. It works the other way round too: whoever has the code at hand and wants the name types the code. The button sits where the cadastral code has somewhere to go, that is on the building's record and on the unit's.

THE FIELD STAYS FREE, AND THAT IS THE IMPORTANT PART. It is not a dropdown. The list of municipalities is not a fixed table: municipalities merge, change name, some change code. A list loaded once and forgotten will, two years from now, suggest codes of municipalities that no longer exist — and a wrong value suggested by the program is worse than an empty field, because whoever enters it trusts it.

SO THE FIELD KEEPS ACCEPTING WHATEVER you type, the dialog says so plainly, and at the bottom it states the date the list is current to. If a municipality is not found the program does not insist: it says it may have been merged or renamed after that date, and invites you to type it by hand.

FINDING MUNICIPALITIES BY THE NAMES PEOPLE ACTUALLY USE. «Spezia» did not find La Spezia and «Reggio Emilia» did not find Reggio nell'Emilia: 2,687 municipalities out of 7,894 have a multi-word name. «Sant'Agata» typed with a phone's curly apostrophe found nothing, and neither did «Sant Agata» without one: 314 municipalities have an apostrophe in their name. «Forli» without the accent did not find Forlì. All of these now work.

AND WHAT YOU TYPED IN FULL COMES FIRST: searching «Roma» there are 42 municipalities containing those letters — Barbarano Romano, Roccaromana — and Roma is the first. If there are too many results the dialog says so instead of showing twenty in silence: «Showing the first 20 of 214». The 121 bilingual municipalities are found in either language: searching «Aldein» finds Aldino.

WHERE THE LIST COMES FROM. From ISTAT, and this is where a trap was hiding. At the same address the institute publishes two files that are not the same list: the one you find first is stuck at January 2024, the other is current but opening it takes 142 MB of memory — which dies on most shared hosting. We converted the right one, once, and the list travels ready-made inside the program: no installation pays that cost and none depends on a connection for a feature that must always be there. Anyone who does not want to wait for a new version can update it themselves with «php artisan kondomanager:aggiorna-comuni --da=list.json».
NOTE: THE ISTAT LIST DOES NOT CONTAIN THE POSTCODE, in either of its forms. That field stays hand-written, and it was worth saying rather than leaving it to be discovered.

THE REST. A municipality's name is now shown as it is written: it used to pass through a function that capitalises every word, which does not work on Italian names — «Reggio nell'Emilia» became «Reggio Nell'emilia» and «L'Aquila» became «L'aquila», across 1,145 names. The program supplied the right name and then rewrote it wrong on the first save. On a unit's record, when both the internal number and the name are missing, the unit's code now appears instead of its internal archive number: that is what the program already claimed to do. And the monospaced font is gone from the unit's cadastral data.
